q: State the rate of identical twins in 2000.
Describe the trend in non-identical twins.
It rose from 6 to 13 per 1000 (1980–2010), then fell slightly to 11.5.
Explain why identical twin numbers stayed the same.
Identical twins come from one egg splitting by chance, which is not affected by age or treatments.
Suggest two reasons for the rise in non-identical twins, and one for the fall after 2010.
Older mothers (more likely to release two eggs) and IVF with several embryos. The fall: IVF clinics now usually put back only one embryo.
